headline: Early galaxies are heavier than we thought
standfirst: Astronomers found hidden stars that change our view of the early universe.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Astronomers found that early galaxies contain far more small stars than previously believed.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Past measurements missed these small stars, leading researchers to underestimate total galaxy mass.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This discovery forces us to rethink our current theories on how the first galaxies formed.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future studies will test if these massive early galaxies fit into our existing cosmic models.

caption:
Astronomers have discovered hidden stars in early galaxies that change what we know about the universe.

These findings suggest that some of the oldest galaxies are much heavier than initial measurements indicated. This forces scientists to reconsider long-held theories about how the early universe developed. It is a major shift in our understanding of cosmic history.
